{"text":"Build S.E.N.T.I.N.E.L., a working offline-first emergency app 

DESIGN: Premium mobile UI, navy #101C2C, white, emergency red #E53935, green online, amber offline. Rounded cards, Inter, Lucide icons, accessible buttons. Bottom nav: Home, Map, First Aid, Bot, Settings.

HOME: Logo, greeting, persistent ONLINE/OFFLINE chip, huge red SOS button with 3-second hold, progress ring, visible cancel, confirmation and activation states. Shortcuts: Map, Medical ID, Bot, First Aid. First-aid cards: CPR, Choking, Wound Care, Burns.

MAP: Offline-capable map, user location, shelter/hazard markers, zoom/recenter. Nearest shelter card with distance, availability, directions. Clicking shelters opens detail sheet with address, capacity, facilities, medical aid and navigation.

MEDICAL ID: Editable name, age, blood group, allergies, conditions, medications, emergency contacts, notes. Local save, lock/PIN/biometric demo and QR sharing.

BOT: Interactive first-aid chat with quick prompts. Online enables simulated AI responses and loading. Offline disables chat but provides offline first-aid guides.

FIRST AID: Offline guides for CPR, choking, bleeding, burns, fractures, seizures, heatstroke with step-by-step instructions.

SETTINGS: Language, theme, notifications, Medical ID lock, PIN, biometrics, connectivity toggle, offline map info, About, privacy, disclaimers.

FUNCTIONALITY: Global connectivity state. Offline disables only Bot; map, shelters, Medical ID and guides remain usable. Simulate SOS honestly; queue offline SOS locally. Every action needs loading, success, error, disabled and confirmation states.

TECH: React, TypeScript, Tailwind, Lucide, reusable components, LocalStorage, mock data. All buttons interactive. No fake real emergency communication. Build polished, responsive, working frontend, not static mockups.","providerOptions":{}}

{"text":"I’ll inspect the current Vite scaffold and existing app structure, then implement the full offline-first emergency experience with local persistence and verify it using the repository’s prescribed checks.","textMode":"visible_message"}

{"text":"The implementation will keep critical content available without a network: all shelter/map data and first-aid instructions are bundled, while only simulated bot replies are gated by connectivity; SOS will clearly distinguish simulated online activation from a locally queued offline event.The core app is now implemented across all requested sections, including persistent settings/Medical ID, SOS hold and confirmation flows, shelter detail sheets, step-by-step offline guides, and bot loading/offline states; I’m running formatting and a production build next to catch any TypeScript or styling integration issues.The production build passes; the formatter’s check flag was incompatible with this repository’s script invocation, so I’m applying the prescribed `pnpm format` command directly and rebuilding after formatting.Formatting and the post-format production build both succeed; I’m doing one final interaction-oriented review now, focusing on whether the responsive screens and key state transitions are testable in the running preview before creating the required local version.The final review identified one offline-first gap: Inter was being requested from Google at runtime. I’m replacing that with a bundled Inter package so typography and the full shell remain available on a first offline launch, then I’ll rerun the build and create the local version.","textMode":"visible_message"}

{"text":"Implemented the improved SOS active experience without changing the rest of the app.

### Changes
- Added prominent red **SOS ACTIVE** badge with pulsing indicator.
- Added live `HH:MM:SS` elapsed timer.
- Added simulated location-sharing status and clearly labeled demo coordinates.
- Added connectivity-aware communication states:
  - Online: **Simulated transmission**
  - Offline: **SOS queued locally – awaiting connection**
- Clearly states that no real emergency service was contacted and no actual GPS data was shared.
- Added large red **Cancel SOS** button.
- Added confirmation dialog with:
  - **Continue SOS**
  - **End Simulation**
- Added loading feedback while ending and success notification afterward.
- Ending restores the original Home SOS hold button.

### Verification
- Formatting completed successfully.
- Production build passed with `pnpm build`.
- Automated preview interaction was unavailable because the supervised preview server could not be reached by the browser runner.","textMode":"visible_message"}

{"text":"Update S.E.N.T.I.N.E.L. language settings. Set English as the default language (English US). Replace Spanish and French options with Hindi (हिन्दी). The language dropdown must contain exactly two options: English and हिन्दी (Hindi). When Hindi is selected, translate all app UI text, navigation labels, buttons, SOS statuses, Settings, Map, Medical ID, First Aid, Bot messages, alerts and confirmations into Hindi. English remains the default. Persist language selection using LocalStorage and apply it consistently across every screen without resetting app state. Keep the existing UI design unchanged. Update the existing S.E.N.T.I.N.E.L. app without redesigning its UI.

PERMISSIONS:
Add a first-launch permission onboarding screen explaining and requesting:
- Location: user location and nearby shelters.
- Camera: scan Medical ID QR codes.
- Notifications: emergency and safety alerts.
- Bluetooth: nearby SOS relay connectivity.

Use contextual permission requests, allow Skip, and show Granted, Denied, and Not Requested states. Never claim permission is granted without actual approval.

QR SCANNER:
Add a functional QR scanning screen accessible from Medical ID. Include camera preview, scan frame, flashlight toggle, close button, loading, success and error states. Support scanning Medical ID QR codes and display decoded medical information with consent. If camera access is unavailable, show permission guidance and manual QR image upload option.

SETTINGS:
Add a Permissions section showing Location, Camera, Notifications and Bluetooth statuses. Each has an icon, explanation, status indicator and Manage button. Allow requesting permissions or opening device settings when already denied. Add permission refresh behavior.

REMOVE WORDS:
Remove every visible occurrence of "Demo", "Demo Mode", "Simulation", "Simulated" and similar labels throughout the application. Replace SOS simulation messaging with neutral emergency request statuses such as "SOS activated", "Request pending", "Sent" or "Queued offline". Never claim real emergency dispatch unless actually integrated.

Keep existing navigation, SOS protection, offline map, shelter details, Medical ID, bot, first aid and settings functionality intact. Maintain English default and Hindi optional language support. Make all screens and buttons interactive with clear loading, success and error feedback.","providerOptions":{}}

{"text":"**Exploring permissions management**

I need to look at how permissions statuses work in the Settings section. When access is denied, the "Open settings" button can't really open the device settings web. It might trigger a guidance modal instead, instructing users to navigate to site settings. Browsers often don’t provide a straightforward settings URL. It seems using something like `window.open("about:preferences#privacy", "_blank")` might not be safe or could be blocked across different browsers. So, I should focus on providing clear instructions without actually opening anything.

**Considering translation components**

I'm thinking about creating a generic `T` component using `const t = useT` for every component. It should help render translations, like `t(guide.title)` and for search filtering. When it comes to shelter details, I wonder about handling dynamic phrases with `${}` — will they work with exact replacements? A dictionary might not accommodate that. I could use composition for translating segments. Plus, I need to ensure we include Hindi. I like how `t("7 guides")` maps, so `${steps.length} ${t("steps")}` could work, right?

**Implementing translations**

I'm thinking about how the IconButton labels could be translated directly within the component, and that the toast text is already translated at the source, which is nice. For the bottom navigation, I want to patch components by adding useT and wrapping them. It might be useful to create a global helper that auto-translates any string properties. I should also define a context for this, starting with core/context and SOS to organize everything effectively.

{"text":"Implemented the full S.E.N.T.I.N.E.L. update while preserving the existing design and navigation.

### Language support
- English remains the default with `en-US` document language.
- Language dropdown now contains exactly:
  - English
  - हिन्दी (Hindi)
- Hindi selection translates navigation, SOS flows, Settings, Map, Medical ID, First Aid, bot content, alerts, dialogs, statuses, and accessibility labels.
- Language selection persists in LocalStorage and updates without clearing application state.

### Permission onboarding
- Added first-launch permission onboarding for:
  - Location
  - Camera
  - Notifications
  - Bluetooth
- Each permission is requested contextually through the applicable browser API.
- Supports Granted, Denied, and Not Requested states.
- Includes loading, result feedback, Continue, and Skip.
- Permission state is never shown as granted unless the browser confirms approval.

### Permission settings
- Added a Permissions section containing explanations, icons, statuses, and Manage controls.
- Added permission refresh behavior, including automatic refresh when the app regains focus.
- Denied permissions show browser/device settings guidance.

### QR scanner
- Added a Medical ID QR scanner accessible from Medical ID.
- Includes:
  - Live camera preview
  - Scan frame
  - Continuous QR detection
  - Flashlight control when supported
  - Close control
  - Loading, success, review, and error states
  - Camera permission guidance
  - Manual image upload fallback
- Decoded Medical ID information is reviewed before importing and requires explicit consent.
- Camera streams and scanning timers are cleaned up when leaving the scanner.

### Emergency wording
- Removed all occurrences of the prohibited wording from application source.
- SOS now uses neutral statuses such as:
  - SOS activated
  - Request pending
  - Sent
  - Queued offline
- The app remains honest that it does not dispatch emergency help or transmit actual GPS data.

### Verification
- Production build passes with `pnpm build`.
- Formatting completed successfully.
- Translation coverage audit passed.
- Restricted-word source audit passed.","textMode":"visible_message"}

{"text":"Implemented Microphone permission throughout S.E.N.T.I.N.E.L.

### Added
- Microphone permission in first-launch onboarding.
- Microphone status and Manage control under **Settings → Permissions**.
- Granted, Denied, and Not Requested states.
- Clear denied-permission guidance with access to Settings.
- Voice input button in the First Aid Bot.
- Listening, recording, processing, and error states.
- English and Hindi voice recognition language support.
- Hindi translations for all new microphone UI.
- Automatic cleanup when recording ends or the Bot screen closes.
- Text chat remains fully functional when microphone access or voice recognition is unavailable.
- Audio capture only begins after explicit user interaction.

- `pnpm format` passed.
- `pnpm build` passed.
